To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed technique outperforms the state-of-the-art in the presence of multiple simultaneous HRQs; and (ii) the proposed technique performs as good as the state-of- theart in the presence of a single HRQ, and it can be considered as a valid alternative to the latter.

the proposed compression technique can be successfully applied on real-life data cubes and can significantly speed-up the execution of HRQ, with a performance that can be even comparable or better than the one of traditional techniques.

a) a novel top-down compression method for data cubes in the presence of multiple HRQs is introduced; b) a hierarchical multidimensional data histogram is introduced and assessed; c) a wide experimental evaluation against benchmark and real-life datasets is provided; d) the proposed technique is shown to significantly improve the performance of OLAP queries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new data cube compression technique that can simultaneously accommodate an even larger family of different-in- nature hierarchical range queries.
a new paradigm for the compression of data cubes in the presence of multiple HRQs.
the problem of efficiently storing and querying large multidimensional data sets in a compressed way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed technique can effectively compress the input data cube while preserving its query performance.

, for the first time, a data cube can be compressed in a way that it is able to simultaneously accommodate different-in-nature multiple HRQ, thus allowing the user to evaluate them in a very fast manner.
the proposed top-down data cube compression technique is able to significantly reduce the storage cost of a data cube, while maintaining an excellent query performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is able to compress a data cube in a way that is able to support a large set of HRQ, and that this compression is able to be performed in an effective way, as shown by the experiments.
our technique can effectively support a large class of HRQ in a top-down compression scenario, and that this is achieved with a reasonable query response time and a small storage overhead.
our technique is a promising alternative to traditional data cube compression approaches, especially when multiple HRQ are involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed technique is able to significantly outperform traditional compression techniques in the presence of simultaneous HRQ, while maintaining competitive performances when HRQ are evaluated individually.

, when multiple simultaneous HRQ are to be evaluated against the same data cube, the compression of this cube should be driven by the multiple constraints imposed by these queries, rather than by the space constraint only.
the proposed technique outperforms the state of the art in all the scenarios considered, with a performance gain ranging from a factor 1.5 to a factor 10.
